title: Publish the Streamable HTTP MCP surface on the @moe/mcp root
description:
Objective: make the already-built Streamable HTTP MCP adapter reachable from the @moe/mcp package root, so a consumer can compose it without a deep import.

MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-11 by governor-f70d1157 (D:/projexts/moe-next):
- packages/mcp/package.json exports is exactly { ".": "./src/index.ts" } — one entry, no subpath. A deep import of ./src/http/** is therefore not merely rail-forbidden, it is unresolvable through the package specifier.
- packages/mcp/src/index.ts publishes stdio ONLY: MOE_MCP_PACKAGE_VERSION (:1), a stdio-server block (:3), StdioServerOptions (:10), StdioAuthOutcome + StdioDispatchPort (:11), and two further stdio blocks (:12, :21). Zero HTTP names.
- The HTTP implementation is present and complete under packages/mcp/src/http/: createHttpMcpAdapter (http-server.ts:244), HttpAdapterOptions (http-server.ts:49), HttpMcpAdapter (http-server.ts:58), HttpDispatchPort (http-tool-bridge.ts:46, re-exported http-server.ts:47), HttpAuthOutcome (http-server.ts:47), HttpSessionPort (http-session.ts:55).
- The .js runtime bridges already exist beside every one of those sources (http-server.js, http-session.js, http-tool-bridge.js, http-resume.js), landed by task-17b03331 — so this task adds no bridge, it only re-exports.

Deliverable: extend packages/mcp/src/index.ts with the HTTP value and type surface named above, and pin it with a root-surface test in the style the package already uses (mcp-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts), plus a plain-Node importability probe. A vitest-only proof is NOT sufficient: vitest resolves a NodeNext ".js" specifier back to ".ts", so a green vitest run cannot show the published root actually loads under plain Node. Probe the bare specifier "@moe/mcp" from node and assert each new name is defined.

NOT in scope: behaviour changes to the HTTP server, session or tool bridge; new transports; daemon host wiring; any edit under apps/.

Owned paths: packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.js, and one focused root-surface test under packages/mcp/src/.

Hard dependencies: NONE. This is buildable today and runs in parallel with the Windows Job chain.

WHY THIS TASK EXISTS: task-49ed1e6d73544fc6ae09b3951a573848 (Foundation MCP dispatch host) is BLOCKED on two separate measured causes. One is the Windows chain, ten links deep behind a single in-flight worker. The other is this export gap, which its own block reason states verbatim: "the HTTP MCP surface [must be] published from @moe/mcp root (with its root/runtime test)". Nothing about that second cause depends on the first. Landing it now means that when the chain finally arrives, 49ed1e6d has one blocker left instead of two.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test && pnpm typecheck
definitionOfDone: packages/mcp/src/index.ts re-exports, from the package root, the value createHttpMcpAdapter and the types HttpAdapterOptions, HttpMcpAdapter, HttpDispatchPort, HttpAuthOutcome and HttpSessionPort, each resolved through a NodeNext ".js" specifier into src/http/**.

A root-surface test asserts the published namespace by a HAND-WRITTEN name list, not by iterating the module's own keys. A test that derives its expectation from Object.keys(namespace) passes unchanged when a name is dropped and proves nothing.

A plain-Node probe imports the bare specifier "@moe/mcp" (no deep path, no vitest resolver) and asserts typeof createHttpMcpAdapter === "function". Record the exact command and its output. Because vitest maps ".js" back to ".ts", a green vitest run is NOT evidence for this item.

Each published TYPE is proven reachable by annotating a value with it through the bare specifier and typechecking. A type-only export is invisible to any runtime key/count assertion, so the runtime probe above cannot cover this item.

The stdio surface published before this change is still present and unchanged: assert the pre-existing stdio names alongside the new HTTP ones in the same test, so a re-export that shadows or drops one fails.
No file under packages/mcp/src/http/ and no file under apps/ is modified. Show the diff by explicit pathspec.
pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, run from the repository root so the repo-wide leg is genuinely repo-wide.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3 — the PLAIN-NODE probe of the bare specifier. Extend the existing pattern; do not invent a second one.

packages/mcp/src/mcp-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts already does exactly this: it uses execFile via promisify to spawn a real Node child, and its own header comment states the reason DoD 3 exists — "vitest rewrites a `./foo.js` specifier back to `foo.ts`; Node does not, and --experimental-strip-types strips types without adding TypeScript's .js -> .ts resolution. A missing bridge is therefore invisible to every [vitest run]." Read it fully and follow its shape, including CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS / CHILD_KILL_MS.

The probe must import the BARE SPECIFIER "@moe/mcp" — no deep path, no relative path — and assert typeof createHttpMcpAdapter === "function". Node resolves a package's own name via its "exports" map (self-reference), which is why the bare specifier works from inside the package; if it does not resolve, that is a real finding about the manifest, not a reason to fall back to a relative import.

RECORD THE EXACT COMMAND AND ITS OUTPUT VERBATIM in your completion evidence. DoD 3 asks for it, and a paraphrase is not evidence.

If the probe fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on an http/* path, a bridge is missing after all — report it rather than adding one, since the description states this task adds no bridge.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 4 — prove each published TYPE is reachable, which neither the runtime list nor the Node probe can do.

A type-only export leaves no runtime trace, so every assertion in steps 3 and 4 is blind to it. Prove reachability by ANNOTATING A VALUE with each type through the bare specifier and letting tsc check it:

  import type { HttpAdapterOptions, HttpMcpAdapter, HttpAuthOutcome, HttpDispatchPort, HttpSessionPort } from "@moe/mcp";

then declare one value per type in the test file, annotated with it. Five types, five annotations. Typecheck failing is the assertion — there is nothing to assert at runtime.

Use `import type` from the BARE specifier, not a relative path: the point is that a CONSUMER can reach these names through the package root. A relative import would compile while proving nothing about the published surface, which is the same class of vacuous proof DoD 2 rules out for the runtime list.

If annotating requires constructing a real adapter or session, do not — a declared binding with `null as unknown as T` is sufficient and keeps the test free of behaviour. This item is about reachability, not construction.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 4. Five types imported with `import type { HttpAdapterOptions, HttpAuthOutcome, HttpDispatchPort, HttpMcpAdapter, HttpSessionPort } from "@moe/mcp"` — the BARE specifier, so this proves a CONSUMER reaches them through the package root. Five annotated bindings, no adapter or session constructed.

Two of the five are pinned harder than mere existence, at zero runtime cost:
- `const adapterOptions: HttpAdapterOptions = { dispatchPort, sessionPort };` is a real object literal, so the published HttpDispatchPort and HttpSessionPort must be EXACTLY the types the published options expect. A lookalike republished from somewhere else would fail here, which name-existence alone would not catch.
- `const adapter: HttpMcpAdapter = null as unknown as ReturnType<typeof rootSurface.createHttpMcpAdapter>;` ties the published type to what the published factory actually returns.
The remaining three are `null as unknown as T` per the plan.

TSC IS THE ASSERTION — stated in the file so a later reader does not mistake the runtime line for the proof. The `it` block exists only to keep the bindings live under noUnusedLocals (tsconfig.base.json sets it true, measured in step 1); it asserts the declared count is 5 and nothing more.
